what: Make `extract_article` refuse to connect to loopback, private, link-local or otherwise non-public addresses, checked on the address it connects to and on every redirect, with an explicit `[daemon] fetch_allow_private_hosts` config list as the only exception.
why: Design: docs/work/fetch-address-guard/design.md. Article URLs come from third-party content (HN-submitted links, Reddit post urls), and cerebro sits on the home LAN beside the daemon's API, Home Assistant and the router; today any http(s) link to 127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x or 169.254.169.254 is fetched, stored and sent to the LLM. No current source or stored item is on a private host (cerebro query 2026-10-03).

criteria.given: a local HTTP server that records every request, and an empty allow list
criteria.then: it fails if the server records any request or the result is anything but `fetch_failed` with detail `blocked address` (shown red against the pre-change extractor, which fetches the page); otherwise both are refused before a connection is made

criteria.given: a server on 127.0.0.1 that answers a public-looking request with a redirect to another loopback URL, reached with its first hop allowed and its redirect target's host not allowed
criteria.then: it fails if the redirect target is fetched; otherwise the redirect hop is refused with `blocked address`
it fails if any non-public address is allowed or the public one refused; otherwise every listed non-public address is refused and the connection goes to the same address the check approved

criteria.given: a config.toml with `fetch_allow_private_hosts = ["127.0.0.1"]`, and one without the key
criteria.when: the config loads and the RSS fetcher, Reddit fetcher and refetch extract an article served on 127.0.0.1
criteria.then: it fails if the config without the key fails to load or does not yield an empty list, or if the allowed host is refused; otherwise the allowed host's page is extracted through each caller and the test suite's materialized config lists 127.0.0.1 so existing local-server tests pass unchanged

criteria.given: docs/architecture/boundaries.md and the config template after the change
criteria.when: a reader looks up article fetching and the [daemon] settings
criteria.then: it fails if either omits the guard or the setting; otherwise boundaries.md states that article fetches refuse non-public addresses at connect time except hosts named in `fetch_allow_private_hosts`, and defaults.py documents the key commented out
it fails on any failing check; otherwise its last line is `verify: PASS`

outOfScope: A feed whose entries link to pages on the operator's own network yields title-only items until those hosts are added to `fetch_allow_private_hosts`; no current source does.
A request through an HTTP proxy is checked against the proxy's address, not the final site; cerebro uses no proxy.
stakes: `extract_article` never connects to a loopback, private, link-local or otherwise non-public address unless its hostname is named in `fetch_allow_private_hosts`.
The address checked is the address connected to, and every redirect hop is checked.
A refused fetch is recorded as `fetch_failed` with detail `blocked address`.
The only way to allow a private host is naming it in config.toml; no environment variable or default allows one.
